elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "no such approval shall be required for an assignment by Client to a financially responsible affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: "Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights ... without the prior written approval of the other party" with the carve-out now limited to "assignment by Client"

elements.element: Customer consent not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Client's approval of any assignment or transfer by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor never to assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall not assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement to a competitor of Client"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "A change of control of Client shall not constitute an assignment or transfer ... and shall not give TrueLink any right to terminate this Agreement"

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: successor carve-out is limited to "an assignment by Client"; TrueLink has no successor right
no notice mechanic appears in the redlined clause

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Client's approval of any assignment or transfer by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld"

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are present: Customer affiliate and successor assignment carve-out, Vendor assignment subject to Customer consent, reasonableness standard on that consent, express bar on Vendor assignment to a Customer competitor, and change-of-control expressly not an assignment and no Vendor termination right.

The edit preserves the original sentence verbatim and adds only the successor language plus one short sentence; the whole-paragraph replace changes nothing beyond the necessary insertion, so minimality holds.
Fallback is not independently satisfied (no mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic), but the locked preferred level is met, so this is immaterial.
No undefined terms, contradictions or dangling mechanics; the pre-existing "financially responsible affiliate" qualifier and all other terms remain effective.
